entities.summary: Christopher Lekapenos was the eldest son of Emperor Romanos I Lekapenos and co-emperor of the Byzantine Empire from 921 until his death in 931. He was given the position of megas hetaireiarches in spring 919, after Romanos assumed guardianship of the underage Emperor Constantine VII. Romanos, who made himself co-emperor in 920, raised Christopher to co-emperor on 21 May 921 to give his family precedence over Constantine VII's Macedonian line. In 928, Christopher's father-in-law, Emperor Nikephoros II Phokas, sent him to conquer the theme of Peloponnese, which he successfully did in 929, securing a crucial victory for the Byzantine Empire. This campaign not only expanded the empire's borders but also showcased Christopher's military prowess and strategic thinking. The consequences of Christopher's military successes were far-reaching, leading to increased stability and growth in the Byzantine Empire, as well as strengthening the family's position within the imperial hierarchy. The legacy of Christopher Lekapenos can be seen in the continued importance of the Byzantine Empire's military and administrative structures, as well as the enduring influence of the Lekapenos family on Byzantine politics and culture. Christopher's achievements serve as a testament to the power of strong leadership and strategic decision-making in shaping the course of human history. Christopher Lekapenos's remarkable life, marked by both triumph and tragedy, continues to captivate historians and scholars today, offering valuable insights into the complexities of Byzantine politics and the evolution of the empire's institutions.
